newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-CRUZEIRO OVERCOME GREMIO IN BRUISING QUARTER-FINAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CRUZEIRO OVERCOME GREMIO IN BRUISING QUARTER-FINAL.

text.p: Cruzeiro overcame fellow Brazilians Gremio in a bruising and unsavoury Libertadores Cup encounter on Tuesday to reach the competition's semi-finals.
Cruzeiro, champions in 1976, went through 3-2 on aggregate despite losing Tuesday's second leg 2-1 away to Gremio, winners in 1995 and semi-finalists last year.
However, neither team really deserved to remain in the competition after a 61-foul match in which the finer arts of the game were put to one side in favour of rough-arm tactics.
Ignoring the best traditions of Brazilian soccer, the teams adopted a cynical approach and concentrated their energies on kicking, provoking and threatening opponents.
Chile's Colo Colo, Cruzeiro's semi-final opponents next month, will be well advised to ensure their first aid kit is well stocked before visiting Brazil.

Cruzeiro increased their aggregate lead when Fabinho, who was limping with a hamstring injury and about to be substituted, found enough energy to get forward and knock in a far-post cross on the hour.

Gremio, who had received six red cards in their previous nine games in the competition, staged a late fightback when former Brazil international Mauro Galvao and Ze Alcino scored twice in three minutes.
Even coach Evaristo Macedo was banned from the touchline after an incident in a previous round when he was also sent off.
The game was best symbolised, however, by the television picture which caught Gremio midfielder Joao Antonio with his arm around an opponent's neck in the first half.
